Andrew Wiles is a mathematician. In 2018, Wiles was appointed the first Regius Professor of Mathematics at Oxford.
What is the atomic number of Plutonium?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
What is the atomic number of Rhenium?
Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
In what year was Isaac Newton born?
Isaac Newton: Newton contributed to and refined the scientific method, and his work is considered the most influential in bringing forth modern science.
In what year was LSD discovered?
LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Tupolev Tu-204: Kazan Aircraft Production Association. It was developed for Aeroflot as a replacement for the medium-range Tupolev Tu-154 trijet in the 1990s.
HTML: United Kingdom. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
Who is credited with discovering Moscovium?
Moscovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Who is credited with discovering Oxycodone?
Oxycodone: Martin Freund. It is a highly addictive and commonly abused drug.
Who is credited with discovering Germanium?
Germanium: Clemens Winkler. Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
Bred for strength and endurance to haul heavy loads across the snow, this large sled-dog breed shares its arctic heritage with breeds like the Siberian Husky and Samoyed — what breed is it?
Alaskan Malamute is a large breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.
Famed for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, this French mathematician was also a principal founder of the secretive Bourbaki group — who was he?
André Weil (6 May 1906 - 6 August 1998) was a French mathematician, known for his foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry.
This deciduous shrub genus in the rose family comes in black, red, and hybrid purple berry varieties, all bitter enough to usually be processed rather than eaten fresh — which genus?
Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
These nocturnal blood-feeding insects from the genus Cimex can trigger skin rashes, itching, and even psychological distress from their bites — what are they commonly called?
Bed bug are insects from the genus Cimex, which are parasites that feed on blood, usually at night.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Made of DNA wound around histone proteins, this substance shapes chromosomes into their distinctive forms during cell division and gatekeeps access to genes for transcription and repair — what is it?
Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein responsible for condensing and packaging chromosomal DNA.
Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Unrelated to poor hygiene, this scalp condition causes flaking and mild itching and is often treated with antifungal or keratolytic remedies; about half of all adults experience it. What is it?
Dandruff is a skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
Native to western North America, this towering conifer is also nicknamed Oregon pine or Columbian pine, though it isn't truly a pine at all — which tree?
Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) is an evergreen conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae.
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows elsewhere in the body—often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvis—affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. What is this condition?
Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium - the lining of the uterus (womb) - grows elsewhere in the body.

This suborder of meat-eating mammals groups together the 'cat-like' carnivorans — cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids — in contrast to their 'dog-like' counterparts in the other major suborder. What suborder is this?
Feliformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "cat-like" carnivorans, including cats, hyenas, mongooses, viverrids, and related taxa.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
This usually benign tumor made of blood vessels typically appears on a baby's skin at birth or within weeks, often on the face, scalp, chest, or back, then shrinks over childhood — what is it?
Hemangioma is a usually benign vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Sold as a 3 percent solution for the bathroom cabinet but explosive when concentrated, this oxidizer and antiseptic carries the formula H2O2 — what is it?
Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2.
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.

A civil engineer who commanded the Australian Corps in 1918, this WWI general was called by historian A. J. P. Taylor 'the only general of creative originality produced by the First World War' — who was he?
John Monash (27 June 1865 - 8 October 1931) was an Australian military commander of the First World War and a civil engineer.

Named after a French mathematician but reportedly learned from his Swiss tutor, this calculus theorem evaluates tricky limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator — what is it called?
L'Hôpital's rule (loh-pee-TAHL) is a mathematical theorem used for evaluating the limit of a quotient of two functions, each of which tends to zero or infinity, by taking each function's derivative.
This common, soft, movable, painless growth made of fatty tissue usually forms just under the skin, often on the back, shoulders, or abdomen — name this benign tumor?
Lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat tissue. The first use of the term "lipoma" to describe these tumors was in 1709.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.
Classified by carbon count into trioses, pentoses, hexoses, and more, these colorless, water-soluble simple sugars are the basic building blocks of carbohydrates — what are they called?
Monosaccharide (from Greek monos: single, sacchar: sugar), also called simple sugars, are a class of organic compounds usually with the formula (CH2O)x.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Combining medicine with comedy, this physician organizes volunteers to clown around for orphans and patients worldwide through a nonprofit institute he founded in 1989 — who is he?
Patch Adams (born May 28, 1945) is an American physician, comedian, social activist, clown, and author.
This bird genus, part of the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, encompasses the living flamingo species — which genus?
Phoenicopterus is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae.

First domesticated by ancient peoples of the Iranian plateau roughly 5,000 years ago, this deciduous shrub bears a fruit rich in symbolic and mythological meaning across many cultures — name the fruit?
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5-5 metres (5-16 ft) tall.
Like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star is only visible from Earth when its beam of radiation sweeps directly toward us — what's the object?
Pulsar (pulsating star, on the model of quasar) is a highly magnetized rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles.

One of the rarest and most valuable precious metals, this hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with only one naturally occurring isotope is prized for enhancing jewelry — what's the element (symbol Rh, atomic number 45)?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Arising from connective tissues like bone, cartilage, muscle, and fat, this rare cancer of mesenchymal cells makes up just 1% of adult diagnoses but 15% of childhood ones. What is it?
Sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that arises from cells of mesenchymal origin.
Despite its long-nosed, mouse-like look, this small mammal is actually a closer cousin to hedgehogs and moles than to rodents — what is it?
Shrew (family Soricidae) are small mole-like mammals classified in the order Eulipotyphla.
Doctors examine the color of this coughed-up airway mucus — greenish or yellow tints can hint at infection, though not which organism caused it — what is it?
Sputum is mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways (the trachea and bronchi).
This Polish far-right entrepreneur and tax advisor placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing a libertarian party and co-leading a far-right coalition — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen (born 20 November 1986) is a Polish far-right politician, entrepreneur and tax advisor.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.
This broad category of large, hoofed mammals was reclassified in 2001 into a new clade after genetic data revealed the older grouping wasn't a true evolutionary lineage. Name the category of animals?
Ungulate are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
This German hunting-dog breed, recognized in 1891, is so much a working dog that in its homeland it's considered unsuitable simply as a house pet — name the breed?
Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Comprising more than 140 species across 16 genera, this small, oily forage fish is found everywhere from the Atlantic to the Black Sea — what is it?
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?

One of its founders, James Keeler, said this science 'seeks to ascertain the nature of the heavenly bodies... rather than their positions or motions' — studying everything from the Sun to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Also called Asian sea bass, this catadromous fish is widely distributed from the Middle East across South and Southeast Asia to Oceania — which fish?
Barramundi: Species of fish. The species is widely distributed in the Indo-West Pacific, spanning the waters of the Middle East, South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania.
This field covers physiological traits like fingerprints and iris patterns, plus behavioral ones like typing rhythm and gait, all used to identify people — what is it called?
Biometrics: Metrics related to human characteristics.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
First classified by Linnaeus in 1753 and indigenous to Eastern Asia, this annual flowering plant has been cultivated throughout history for fiber, oil, food, and medicine — which plant?
Cannabis sativa: Plant species. It has been cultivated throughout recorded history and used as a source of industrial fiber, seed oil, food, and medicine.

Named from a Latin word meaning 'blind,' this pouch at the start of the large intestine sits on the same side of the body as the appendix and receives chyme straight from the small intestine — which structure?
Cecum: Pouch in the large intestine. It is typically located on the right side of the body (the same side of the body as the appendix, to which it is joined).
Traceable to fairy tales that weren't classified this way until the seventeenth century, this genre spans picture books for toddlers to young-adult fiction for teens — what category of writing?
Children's literature: Stories, books, magazines, and poems primarily written for children.
This spore-forming, rod-shaped bacterium produces the most potent toxin known to science, causing a severe paralytic illness often linked to bulging canned food — what's its name?
Clostridium botulinum: Species of endospore forming bacterium.
Named from ancient Greek for 'footless' after being mistaken for a legless swallow, this bird's closest relatives are actually hummingbirds — and it almost never touches the ground. Which bird?
Common swift: Species of bird. The resemblances between the groups are due to convergent evolution, reflecting similar contextual development.
Unknown in the wild, this cultivated autumn-flowering plant has had its dried stigmas prized as the world's priciest spice for over 3,500 years — what is its scientific name?
Crocus sativus: Species of flowering plant. Crocus sativus, commonly known as saffron crocus or autumn crocus, is a species of flowering plant in the iris family Iridaceae.
Introduced in 1984, this turboprop regional airliner series was developed from an earlier company model and later gained 'Quiet' variants with active noise-cancellation — which aircraft family?

De Havilland Canada Dash 8: Canadian turboprop airliner. The De Havilland Canada DHC-8, commonly known as the Dash 8, is a series of turboprop-powered regional airliners, introduced by de Havilland Canada (DHC) in 1984.

The largest collection of fossils from this extinct Ice Age canine came from the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, though it roamed from South American savanna to North American forested mountains — what animal was it?
Dire wolf: Extinct species of canine mammal.
This condition involves involuntarily repeating words or sounds spoken by someone else, and is commonly seen in autism, ADHD, and Tourette syndrome. What is it called?

This is the process of creating economic value by spotting and commercializing opportunities — typically demanding considerable initiative and bearing real risk in exchange for most of the reward. What's the term?
Entrepreneurship: Taking financial risks in the hope of profit.
Also known by the scientific name Gyps fulvus, this large Old World bird of prey belongs to the family Accipitridae — which species is it?
Eurasian griffon vulture: Species of bird. It is also known as the Eurasian griffon or griffon vulture, although the latter term is sometimes used for the genus Gyps as a whole.
This centuries-old number theory statement claims there are no positive whole-number solutions to a^n + b^n = c^n whenever the exponent exceeds two — what's it called?
Fermat's Last Theorem: 17th-century conjecture proved by Andrew Wiles in 1994.
This American chemical engineer at Caltech won the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for pioneering 'directed evolution' to engineer enzymes — and later joined Alphabet's board — who is it?
Frances Arnold: American chemist and academic (born 1956)
Once Mexico's top law-enforcement official as secretary of public security, this man was convicted in a Brooklyn courtroom in 2023 for taking millions in bribes from the Sinaloa Cartel — who is he?
Genaro García Luna: Mexican politician and convicted felon (born 1968)
With the symbol Au and atomic number 79, this soft, dense element is so unreactive that only platinum sits below it — and it often turns up as native nuggets in riverbeds. What is it?
Gold: Chemical element with atomic number 79 (Au). Chemically, gold is a transition metal, a group 11 element, and one of the noble metals.

This French civil engineer made his name building railway bridges like the Garabit Viaduct and later helped erect the Statue of Liberty, before retiring to study meteorology and aerodynamics — who was he?

A pioneer of modern control theory whose collaboration with Claude Shannon helped lay the foundations of the Information Age, he also helped design the automatic guns that defended London from V-1 flying bombs — who was he?
Hendrik Wade Bode: American scientist and engineer (1905–1982)
A pungent root vegetable in the same family as mustard, wasabi, and cabbage, this spice is likely native to Southeastern Europe and Western Asia — what is it?
Horseradish: Species of flowering plants in the cabbage family Brassicaceae.
This mammal order today includes only small African and Middle Eastern hyraxes, but once boasted a species weighing up to 600 kilograms called Titanohyrax — which order?
Hyracoidea: Order of mammals. It includes the living hyraxes, placed within the family Procaviidae, and several extinct taxa.
Known historically as green vitriol or copperas, this blue-green heptahydrate salt is used to treat anemia and forms a paramagnetic octahedral complex in water — which compound?
Iron(II) sulfate: Chemical compound. Iron(II) sulfate or ferrous sulfate (British English: sulphate instead of sulfate) denotes a range of salts with the formula FeSO4·xH2O.
Despite its name, this is actually a species of sunflower native to central North America, grown across temperate zones for its edible tuber — also called a sunchoke. What is it?
Jerusalem artichoke: Species of sunflower native to eastern North America. It is cultivated widely across the temperate zone for its tuber, which is used as a root vegetable.
The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, she served as a mission specialist on two Space Shuttle Columbia flights, the second ending in the 2003 disaster that killed her — who was she?
About 1.5 metres long and beginning at the cecum via the ileocecal valve, this final section of the human gut absorbs water and salt before waste reaches the rectum — what part of the body is it?
Large intestine: Last part of the digestive system in vertebrates.
The only person ever to win two unshared Nobel Prizes, this American chemist earned one for his work on the chemical bond and another for peace activism — who is he?
Linus Pauling: American scientist and activist (1901–1994)
This American experimental physicist won the 1968 Nobel Prize for discovering resonance states using the hydrogen bubble chamber — who was he?
Luis Walter Alvarez: American physicist, inventor and professor (1911–1988)
Native to the Malay Peninsula and Borneo, this tropical fruit hides sweet, tangy white flesh beneath a deep reddish-purple rind — which fruit?
Mangosteen: Tropical evergreen tree with edible fruit.
Combined with formaldehyde to create hardwearing resins found in Formica countertops, plastic dinnerware, and the foam in a Magic Eraser, this nitrogen-rich compound also resists fire — what is it?
Melamine: Fire-resistant chemical used in dinnerware, insulation, and cleaning products.
Often striking one side of the head and sometimes preceded by a sensory 'aura,' this neurological disorder brings nausea and sensitivity to light and sound — what is it?
Migraine: Disorder resulting in recurrent moderate–severe headaches.
Sold under the brand name Singulair, this asthma medication blocks leukotriene D4 in the lungs but received a UK black box warning in 2019 over neuropsychiatric side effects — what is it?
Montelukast: Medication used in asthma or COPD.

The first production helicopter with fully fly-by-wire flight controls, this European twin-engine military chopper comes in troop-transport and naval anti-submarine variants flown by over a dozen NATO nations. What is it?
NHIndustries NH90: Family of military helicopters.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandins, though it carries a notable risk of liver problems — what is it?
Nimesulide: Anti-inflammatory drug. Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.
First described in 1689 by a local naturalist, this aquatic cave-dwelling salamander is the only exclusively cave-dwelling chordate native to Europe — what is it?
Britain, Germany, and Italy jointly built this twin-engine, variable-sweep-wing combat jet through a tri-national consortium, first flying it in 1974 — which aircraft?
Panavia Tornado: Family of multi-role combat aircraft.
This bony ring connects the spine to the lower limbs at the hip joints, formed by the sacrum, coccyx, and a pair of hip bones — what body region?
Pelvis: Lower torso of the human body.

So reactive that it never appears uncombined in nature, this element was famously isolated in 1669 by Hennig Brand — the scientific community's first documented discovery of an element — and comes in white and red forms. Which one is it?
Phosphorus: Chemical element with atomic number 15 (P)
This plant process moves pollen from an anther to a stigma, eventually letting a tube grow down the style to reach the ovary and enable fertilization. What is it?
Pollination: Biological process occurring in plants.
Discovered in 1915, this red dwarf is the closest star to Earth besides the Sun, orbiting its two larger neighbors once every 550,000 years — which star?
Proxima Centauri: Nearest star to the Solar System.
The sole member of its genus and a relative of apples and pears, this hard, aromatic golden fruit is too tart to enjoy raw but turns lovely as jam or a fragrant cheese — what is it?
With the widest geographic range of any non-human primate, this brown-to-grey Old World monkey lives in matrilineal troops of up to 200 individuals — which species?
Rhesus macaque: Species of Old World monkey. The rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta), colloquially rhesus monkey, is a species of Old World monkey in the Macaca genus.
What term describes herbivorous mammals like cattle and giraffes that digest plant matter by regurgitating and re-chewing it as cud?
Ruminant: Hoofed herbivorous grazing or browsing mammals.
In this thought experiment a hypothetical cat in a closed box may be considered simultaneously alive and dead. Which quantum concept is it illustrating?
In quantum mechanics, Schrödinger's cat is a thought experiment concerning quantum superposition, in which a hypothetical cat in a closed box may be considered simultaneously alive and dead.
Called the 'father of modern differential geometry,' this Chinese-born American mathematician and poet was honored with a medal the IMU named after him in 2010 — who is he?

Shiing-Shen Chern: Chinese-American mathematician and poet. Shiing-Shen Chern (Chinese: 陳省身; pinyin: Chén Xǐngshēn; October 26, 1911 – December 3, 2004) was a Chinese-born American mathematician and poet.

Native to Eurasia and found in Paleolithic-era deposits in ancient Britain, this flowering plant's ripe berries and cooked leaves are eaten in some regions despite its nightshade family's fearsome reputation — what is it?
Solanum nigrum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family. The plant was known and mentioned by ancient herbalists, including Dioscorides.
Shaped roughly like a necktie and made up of the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process, which flat bone protects the heart and lungs at the front of the rib cage?
Sternum: Flat bone in the middle front part of the rib cage.

Caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum, this infection famously hides: a painless ulcer first, then a rash that loves the palms and soles, then years of silent latency before tertiary damage. What is it?

This congenital heart defect combines four distinct abnormalities — including a hole between the ventricles and a narrowed pulmonary exit — and can trigger cyanotic 'spells' in infants — what is this condition?
Tetralogy of Fallot: Type of congenital heart defect. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), formerly known as Steno-Fallot tetralogy, is a congenital heart defect characterized by four specific cardiac defects.
This white compound found in sunscreen, paint, and food coloring under the number E171 makes up two-thirds of all pigments used worldwide and is valued at over $13 billion — what is it?
Titanium dioxide: Chemical compound. Titanium dioxide, also known as titanium(IV) oxide or titania, is the inorganic compound derived from titanium with the chemical formula TiO2.
Nicknamed 'Crusty' by NATO, this twin-engined Soviet airliner featured a glazed nose and could operate from unpaved airfields — which aircraft is it?
Described from Mongolian fossils in 1924 and smaller than relatives like Deinonychus, which feathered, sickle-clawed dinosaur genus roamed Late Cretaceous Asia?
Velociraptor: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur. The type species is V. mongoliensis, named and described in 1924.
A slow-moving filter-feeder and the largest known fish alive — the biggest reliably recorded stretched nearly 19 metres — this is the only living member of its family. What is it?
Whale shark: Largest living species of fish. The whale shark (Rhincodon typus) is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known extant fish species.
These striped African equines share their genus with horses and asses, and the leading theory says their patterns evolved mainly to deter biting flies — what are they?
Zebra: Striped animal in the equid family.
What is the chemical symbol for bohrium?
The symbol for bohrium is Bh. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
